title: Mina and the Traveling Water
markdown:
In a peaceful village between soft green hills lived Mina, a girl who loved maps. Her friends were Fern, a curious fox, and Captain Ivo, a sailor. Mina’s room was filled with maps of roads, oceans, and clouds, and even the kettle seemed to know it was being watched.

One warm morning, they found their rain barrel nearly empty. The garden plants looked thirsty, leaves hanging like tired flags. “Where has the water gone?” wondered Fern.

Mina traced a water droplet on her map. “It seems like there isn’t much left,” she whispered. They tried digging, but it didn’t help. The soil was just soil, and the barrel stayed a quiet wooden circle.

“Water is a traveler with a great sense of adventure,” Captain Ivo said, looking at the blue sky.

Fern wondered if it visited friends in the soil. Mina, looking at her sky map, asked, “Captain Ivo, are the clouds made of water?”

As the sun warmed the little water left in the barrel, they watched, wide-eyed, as it shimmered and rose up like tiny whispers on the breeze. A bright bead sat on the rim, then thinned, then was not a bead at all. “The sun tickles the water, and it flies away!” gasped Fern.

Captain Ivo smiled. “Water travels up into the clouds.”

Mina’s eyes lit up. She tapped a fluffy cloud on her map. “So the water goes up to make clouds! They gather to make a soft pillow in the sky, and then they let the water fall back down!”

“How do we know when?” asked Fern.

Mina pointed to a large puffy cloud moving closer. “This cloud looks very full,” she said, “and the wind is pushing it this way.” They heard a soft distant rumble, like a gentle whisper from a friend who was almost home.

They made sure the rain barrel was ready, lid off, mouth open, waiting. Soon a tiny droplet landed on Mina’s nose. Then another. Gentle rain began to fall, filling the barrel with a small happy music. The garden plants perked up, and the flowers lifted their faces as if someone had remembered their names.

“We did it!” cheered Fern.

Captain Ivo smiled. “Water takes a long journey. It goes up to the clouds, and then it comes back down. It’s a wonderful, never-ending circle.”

Mina drew a big arrow on her sky map. “It’s the water cycle,” she announced. “The water visits the sky and then comes back home.”

The rain kept whispering. Mina wondered what other journeys were already drawn on maps she had not made yet—another droplet, another pillow in the sky, another quiet return to the barrel.
characters: Mina (map reader), Fern (curious fox), Ivo (sailor captain)
